sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Oversized Furniture and Home Decor

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union
Agreement between Canada and the People's Republic of China for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (2014)
Convention between Canada and the United States of America with Respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (1980, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended, and its Regulations (SOR/2002-184); Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, Part 18.1 (ss. 119.1-119.6), establishing the Register of Individuals with Significant Control at the 25% threshold; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Part 2 as to money laundering and financing offences; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Freezing Assets of Corrupted Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 13.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Statement of Beneficial Ownership identifying each individual with significant control (25% or greater)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or authorized officer of the parent entity; local registrar of companies for the entity shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if originating jurisdiction is a Hague Convention signatory) or Consular Legalization by the Embassy/Consulate of Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies and proof of residential address for each individual director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or Commissioner for Oaths in the individual's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via the designated competent authority of the state of issuance or Canadian Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source of wealth confirmation for each UBO and corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing financial institution under applicable AML/KYC client identification standards
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (where the bank or employer jurisdiction requires it)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-clearance of all shareholders, UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against the FINTRAC-based PEP database, Global Affairs Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, and the OFAC SDN List where US-dollar payment rails (Stripe, Affirm BNPL) are used. Enhanced customer due diligence including documented source of funds is required for foreign PEPs. Screening reports must be completed before incorporation and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry - via https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry (operated by Service Alberta and authorized registry agents)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Alberta corporate names must use Roman (Latin) script and be in English or French. A non-Latin script name, such as Chinese characters, is not registrable unless converted into a transliterated English or French form, which then becomes the legal name and must be screened through NUANS. An Unlimited Liability Corporation must include the legal element 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Corporation'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be renewed for an additional period before expiry through the Alberta Corporate Registry. If a proposed name is rejected, the applicant or its registry agent must submit a written request for reconsideration to the Director of the Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of the rejection, accompanied by the NUANS report, a revised name where appropriate, and written submissions establishing distinctiveness and absence of prohibited or misleading tokens. The Director will issue a written decision; a final refusal may be challenged by judicial review in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for an Alberta ULC provided the registered office is a physical street address within Alberta, not a post office box, and is capable of accepting service of process; a licensed registered agent or law firm office satisfies this requirement. A virtual or co-working address is acceptable for incorporation, but a municipal business licence and physical presence may be required if warehousing or freight handling of oversized furniture commences in Alberta.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated <5% annual probability) for a non-regulated e-commerce retail structure; Alberta Corporate Registry does not conduct routine unannounced inspections for a holding or low-risk online retail ULC, but inspections may occur upon regulatory complaint, abandoned address reports, or municipal by-law checks if local operations exist.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (via authorized NUANS intermediary)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee schedule under the Alberta Corporate Registry tariff

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 8, 10, 101-102, 212-213; Alberta Corporations Regulation, AR 70/2001; conditional registration under the Upholstered and Stuffed Articles Act, RSA 2000, c U-6 for upholstered inventory
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Registrar of Corporations); filings accepted through authorized Alberta Registry Agents or the online Corporate Registry service
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1 under the ABCA) together with notice of registered office and first directors
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed by Alberta law; shares may be subscribed at nominal value, and no escrow or capital-impairment account is required. For U.S. check-the-box pass-through planning, contemporaneous capital-account documentation is recommended.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Articles of Incorporation filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry are hereby ratified, and the subscriptions for the issued Common Shares set out in the register of members are hereby accepted. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation be and is hereby fixed at [full street address], Alberta, Canada, and the corporate minute book and records shall be maintained at that address. RESOLVED, that [Name] be and is hereby appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Chief Financial Officer, each to hold office until replacement or resignation. RESOLVED, that the directors are authorized to open Canadian-currency bank accounts, execute banking resolutions, and complete all statutory registrations necessary to give effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Name Search and Name Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) via an authorized Registry Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS full-name search for the proposed corporate name (e.g., '[Name] Unlimited Liability Corporation' or '[Name] ULC'); optionally obtain a Name Approval reservation; confirm that the name does not conflict with existing trademarks or registered corporate names and that the designator 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' is included; a numbered company (e.g., '[number] Alberta Ltd.') remains available if a name reservation is not desired.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and up to three alternatives
Proof of 9-1-1 civic address for the proposed registered office
Instruction letter to the Registry Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, a fresh NUANS search with a substituted name is filed; name reservations are valid for 90 days and may be renewed once.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Articles of Incorporation and Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel or corporate services provider acting for the incorporator(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation under the ABCA specifying share classes, the unlimited liability status of the ULC, optional transfer restrictions, the Alberta registered address, and the consent of the first directors; prepare the subscription documents and confirm the unlimited liability exposure of shareholders in the explanatory minutes.
required_dossiers: Consent of first director(s) to act in office
Payment instructions for the CAD 150 registry fee
Certificate of status for any corporate incorporator (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Registry corrections are cured by filing prescribed amendments or a Notice of Correction within the statutory cure period; substantive share-structure errors require an Articles of Amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission to the Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Articles of Incorporation through the Registry Agent's online portal; pay the statutory CAD 150 incorporation fee (plus service-agent fees); verify that the NUANS report is not older than 90 days; select the issuance method for the Certificate of Incorporation (electronic or paper).
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report (not older than 90 days)
Consent of directors to act in office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, the Registry issues a notice of defect; counsel refiles corrected Articles within the stated cure period without loss of filing priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Registry Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and the official corporate registry extract (attesting legal name, Alberta corporation number, registered office, and directors); reconcile the corporate access number for future amendments, annual returns, and third-party verifications.
required_dossiers: Corporate key / access code for online filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a clerical error, file a Notice of Correction with the Registrar; certified duplicates are available at a nominal fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting, First Board Resolution and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Alberta ULC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting (in person or by unanimous written resolution); adopt the first board resolution covering share subscription, registered office, and officer appointments; adopt By-law No. 1 on general governance; issue share certificates; maintain the minute book at the registered office; pass the banking resolution for CAD and USD accounts and prepare the merchant-onboarding file for Stripe and Affirm BNPL as part of Stage 3.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defective organizational resolutions are ratified by a corrective board resolution or unanimous shareholder resolution; the minute book must be reconstructed and countersigned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Registration, Provincial and Municipal Licences
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); municipal business licensing office; WCB-Alberta; Service Alberta (conditional consumer licensing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) for corporation income tax, GST/HST (mandatory once gross revenue exceeds CAD 30,000), payroll, and import/export accounts as relevant; obtain the municipal business licence for the principal office and warehouse/dispatch location; open the WCB-Alberta employer account before the first employee is hired; register under the Upholstered and Stuffed Articles Act only if upholstered articles are held for sale.
required_dossiers: Upholstered and Stuffed Articles registration form (conditional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA registration is delayed, business may commence with 'registration pending' status; municipal licence refusals are appealable to the local business licence appeal committee; WCB assessment disputes proceed to the Appeals Commission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No federal or provincial industrial operating licence is mandated for ISIC 4791 e-commerce furniture retail; municipal business licensing is mandatory at the registered place of business, and conditional dealer registration applies under the Upholstered and Stuffed Articles Act (Alberta) if upholstered inventory is sold.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence (e.g., City of Calgary or City of Edmonton); conditional 'Dealer Registration' under the Upholstered and Stuffed Articles Act, RSA 2000, c U-6; no separate federal operating permit is required for this retail classification.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (EPEA); the Impact Assessment Agency of Canada is engaged only for federally listed projects, which do not include furniture warehousing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — retail distribution and finished-furniture storage are not listed activities under the Activities Designation Regulation, AR 276/2003; a Category B Registration would be triggered only by ancillary operations such as an on-site paint/finishing booth, fuel storage above 5,000 L, or vehicle fleet maintenance.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater is generated by finished-furniture storage; floor washwater must meet municipal sewer by-law limits (pH typically 6.0-11.0, TSS, and BOD ceilings); any incidental refinishing must keep VOC emissions below approval thresholds under AR 276/2003; cardboard, pallet, and plastic-film packaging must be recycled under municipal franchise agreements, and waste handling must comply with the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (Alberta) and the Waste Control Regulation, AR 192/1996.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: the warehouse and office occupancy must comply with the Alberta Fire Code (National Fire Code of Canada 2020 - Alberta Edition), including municipal fire inspection clearance, sprinkler coverage where floor areas exceed prescribed thresholds, minimum 6-m clearance aisles for oversized-furniture racking, and unobstructed egress. Structural load: pallet racks, mezzanines, and oversized-furniture storage systems require certification by a registered professional engineer under the Alberta Building Code 2019 (Division B), including seismic, point-load, and overturning reviews. Occupational: WCB-Alberta coverage is mandatory; the workplace must comply with the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Code 2009, including competent operator certification for forklifts, manual-handling limits for oversized goods, first-aid kits, and posted OHS notices.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA) — federal income tax and GST/HST administration; business portals: Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account (MyBA). Alberta corporate income tax is also administered by the CRA under the Alberta Tax Administration Agreement, while customs assessment and import GST enforcement are handled by the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: After Alberta incorporation via the Alberta Corporate Registry (Registry Connect), the ULC obtains a nine-digit federal Business Number (BN). Domestic applicants file Form RC1 (Business Number Registration) through BRO; non-resident applicants use Form RC464 (Request for a Business Number and GST/HST Registration for Non-Residents), filed with CRA's International and Large Business Directorate by mail or courier. The BN is the sole statutory identifier; program accounts are appended as suffixes: RT for GST/HST, RC for corporate income tax, RP for payroll, and RM for import/export. CRA can set the GST/HST registration date retrospectively to the day taxable supplies first exceeded CAD 30,000, and registered entities must display their BN (RT account) on all invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (default): an Alberta ULC is deemed resident in Canada under ITA s. 250(4)(c) and is taxed under Part I on worldwide income. Pass_Through_Eligible: the ULC may elect under ITA s. 34.1 to be treated as a partnership (deemed not to be a corporation), flowing income out to shareholders. Territorial_Scope: residence-based full taxation with foreign tax credits and treaty relief; non-resident shareholders of a ULC face Part XIII withholding and certain dispositions may attract branch tax analysis. Tax_Exempt_Zone: none for ordinary Alberta e-commerce; Alberta has no provincial sales tax, but the federal 5% GST applies and no income-tax holiday zones are available for this activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Alberta ULC s. 34.1 election: the eligible unlimited liability company, jointly with all shareholders, may file a written election with the Minister to be deemed not to be a corporation and to have its business carried on by a partnership composed of its shareholders (pass-through); for GST/HST purposes, the election deems the shareholders to be registrants carrying on the business with joint and several liability. There is no general US-style check-the-box regime in Canadian tax law; however, for US tax purposes the ULC may be treated as a partnership or disregarded entity on Form 8832, and planners must align the US check-the-box result with the ITA s. 34.1 election to avoid hybrid mismatches. The hybrid mismatch rules (ITA s. 18.4) and the excess interest and financing expenses limitation rules (ITA ss. 18.2/18.3) further constrain deduction-stuffing in cross-border ULC financing structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (ETA); Alberta levies no provincial sales tax, so the applicable rate in Alberta is the federal GST at 5% with no HST component, while exports are zero-rated at 0%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold: GST/HST registration becomes mandatory when taxable supplies made in Canada exceed CAD 30,000 in a calendar quarter or in the aggregate over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; however, under the July 1, 2021 platform-economy rules, marketplace facilitators and non-resident sellers using Canadian fulfillment warehouses are deemed suppliers and must register and collect GST/HST without benefit of the small-supplier exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time electronic invoicing, fiscal digital stamping, or continuous transaction control regime applies in Canada. GST/HST invoices require at minimum the supplier name and BN (RT account), recipient name, date, description of supply, consideration, and tax amount (ETA s. 223). E-invoicing is voluntary and interoperable through CRA's Peppol/PINT-based pilot (2024-2026). Import fiscal clearance is electronic through the CBSA Single Window Initiative and the CARM digital platform, with import GST accounted on the customs self-assessment; exporters must file the Canada Export Declaration electronically. Registrants must retain books and records, including underlying export data, for six years, and CRA may require machine-readable formats.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated (0% GST/HST) treatment applies to the export supply of oversized furniture and household goods under ETA Schedule VI, Part V where the sale is made by a registrant, the goods are delivered to a carrier or freight forwarder for shipment outside Canada, they leave Canada in substantially the same condition, and the supplier retains satisfactory documentary evidence of export; ETA Schedule VI, Part VII separately zero-rates services performed on goods that are being exported (e.g., white-glove preparation, packing, and drayage to the US border). Supplies delivered to a Canadian address, or goods exported by the buyer rather than the seller, are not zero-rated and remain taxable at 5%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic filing through the CBSA Canada Export Reporting mechanism, inclusive of the former B13A)
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or courier consignment note showing the outbound international movement
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank confirmation of receipt of foreign-currency export proceeds)
Time-stamped proof of export from the carrier (customs outbound stamp, terminal departure receipt, or GPS/scan trail)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA's GST/HST export verification and refund-integrity programs examine export documentation transaction-by-transaction; fabricated or manipulated evidence results in denial of the 0% rate, reassessment and clawback of any refund with arrears interest, civil penalties under ETA ss. 280-285 including false-statement and culpable-conduct penalties, and gross-negligence penalties under ITA s. 163(2); the four-year normal reassessment period is extended indefinitely where misrepresentation is established, and criminal prosecution for evasion (ETA s. 331, Criminal Code fraud) may follow. Because the entity is an Alberta unlimited liability corporation, each shareholder is jointly and severally personally liable for the ULC's GST/HST debts and clawback amounts, including those arising from invalid export zero-rating claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) in coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and Global Affairs Canada for trade-related sanctions export controls; the Department of Finance Canada oversees the Exchange Fund Account and the Canadian dollar exchange rate regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current and capital account transactions with no general restrictions imposed under the Currency Act, the Bank of Canada Act, or the International Economic and Financial Sanctions regime. There is no requirement for central bank approval for routine cross-border capital transfers, dividends, or profit remittances, provided the transactions are supported by appropriate documentary evidence and comply with anti-money laundering (AML) and know-your-client (KYC) requirements under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). ULC distributions to non-resident shareholders may be characterized as dividends or deemed taxable dividends by the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and are subject to withholding tax under the Canada Income Tax Act, typically reduced to 5% or 0% under an applicable tax treaty if the shareholder is a tax resident of a treaty jurisdiction and provides a valid residency certificate. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal but prudent advance pricing and transfer-pricing documentation are recommended to satisfy CRA's Part XIII withholding and section 247 compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada maintains no statutory requirement for exporters to surrender, sell, or convert export proceeds into CAD within any prescribed timeline. The Income Tax Act and the Customs Act do not impose mandatory conversion ratios on export receipts. Exporters may maintain foreign currency banking accounts with any Canadian banking entity or designated financial institution. All inbound payments must be reported under the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) thresholds and, for statistical purposes, to Statistics Canada via the International Trade Ministerial Reporting Program if transactions exceed CAD 1 million per month. There are no exchange control restrictions on repatriating export proceeds, and hedging instruments are fully accessible.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) - Alberta Market
The Bank of Nova Scotia (Scotiabank) - Alberta Market
Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) - Alberta Market

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) and fintech payment partners have limited viability for onboarding a Canadian ULC as a primary banking partner due to Canada's Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) implemented in November 2024, which mandates Bureau de la concurrence registration with the Bank of Canada (BoC) for any payment service provider operating in or targeting the Canadian market. Offshore EMIs that lack BoC RPAA registration, FINTRAC MSB registration, and physical presence in Canada are legally constrained from processing domestic or cross-border payments directly for a Canadian entity. A practical approach is to use a top-tier Canadian Schedule I bank as the core deposit and clearing bank, and separately onboard a licensed Canadian PSP (e.g., Stripe Canada Ltd., Payoneer Inc. if FINTRAC-registered) solely for e-commerce card settlement and BNPL payment acceptance. The PSP must hold a BoC RPAA registration or operate under an exemption. The ULC must maintain ultimate control over treasury cash flows; funds should be swept continuously to the Schedule I bank clearing account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) of the Alberta ULC are expected to complete a bona-fide identity verification process. While remote onboarding is statutorily permitted under federal AML regulations, all major Canadian banks (RBC, TD, Scotiabank, CIBC, BMO) maintain an internal policy requiring that at least one director or authorized securities administrator attend an in-branch interview in Alberta for the initial deal, or submit to a live video verification interview if the director is a non-resident. For the Capital Escrow Account, physical presence is strongly recommended at the outset. For Operational Accounts, expedited remote onboarding is feasible when the ULC also uses a Canadian-registered agent with an Alberta physical office. IF RARELY, some banks allow full digital onboarding with a notarized corporate certificate and a thorough verification call, but interview mandates are typically high for ULC structures due to the unlimited liability feature and the absence of share certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Delayed/ambiguous UBO chain for a non-resident parent holding the ULC
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a complete organizational chart with all UBOs holding 10% or more direct or indirect ownership; certified copies of passport pages; a copy of the Alberta ULC Articles of Incorporation; a copy of the most recent foreign parent company registry excerpt (e.g., Companies House filing) showing the shareholder chain; and a director resolution affirming source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Online-retail e-commerce risk classification flagged as high volume / low visibility
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a corporate business plan including a description of the oversized furniture fulfillment model, registered trade-trademark or brand registry excerpt, third-party logistics contracts and carrier agreements, supplier invoices, and a projected cash-flow forecast. Provide a sample customer purchase order and proof of legitimate website domain ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual source of wealth for initial capital injection from a non-resident shareholder
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a sworn source-of-wealth statement, audited financial statements of the contributing entity (or personal tax returns if individual), bank references from the remitting foreign bank, and evidence of underlying commercial activity (e.g., sale of overseas furniture inventory, loan drawings from a lending institution).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reputational risk flag due to cross-border freight agent in a high-risk jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the freight forwarder's commercial registration certificate, a valid KYC questionnaire completed by the freight agent, the full trade invoice and bill of lading, and insurance certificates; state the economic rationale, and ensure no ties to sanctioned entities as screened against the OSFI consolidated sanctions list.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FX hedging or derivative documentation insufficient for non-resident guarantee
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply the non-resident parent company's annual report and auditor's opinion, a legal opinion from the parent's home counsel on guarantee enforceability, and a Form 52-109F or equivalent in-kind guaranty certificate for the derivative transactions; ensure the ULC has previously executed an ISDA agreement if borrowing capacity is used.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections into the Alberta ULC should be wired via SWIFT to the designated Tier-1 domestic bank account using the bank's SWIFT BIC and a unique client attribution ID (CA/AB/ULC-style reference). The sender must indicate the appropriate purpose message in the remittance details: either 'Equity injection - capital contribution for general corporate and working capital' (purpose code under the IMF Balance of Payments Manual 6, typically 'D614' for equity capital for direct investment in an enterprise) or 'Loan - shareholder subordinated debt' (code 'D613' for intercompany financing). The bank will request a board resolution approving the capital injection, a shareholder contribution agreement or promissory note for shareholder loans, and a completed FINTRAC 'Large Cash Transaction Report' trigger if payment is over CAD 10,000 or in cash; wire transfers over CAD 30,000 are automatically subjected to FINTRAC catch-all reporting. The ULC must ensure that the incoming wire is not accidentally marked as 'proceeds of trade' for legal goods, which could trigger different anti-money-laundering classification; instead, choose 'equity investment - corporate investment' as legal phraseology. For funds originating from outside Canada, the settlement must clear through a correspondent bank of the remitting institution; a cross-border wire template (SWIFT MT103) with full beneficiary address and account number is mandatory. Verification steps include a written board resolution dated within the last 30 days, financial declarations of the investing entity, and if over CAD 25,000, a Certificate of Compliance under the CRA non-resident entity requirements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements related to cross-border procurement of furniture and freight services, the primary clearing rail is the SWIFT MT103 message for high-value and mid-value transfers routed through the ULC's Schedule I Canadian bank correspondent network. For transactions above CAD 10,000, outbound MT103 must include the full legal name of the beneficiary, the beneficiary's account number (IBAN or domestic account), the beneficiary bank's SWIFT BIC, and the corresponding purpose code (e.g., 'EP' for general trade of goods, 'RD' for repayment of loans). A commercial documentary irrevocable letter of credit (L/C) is permissible for high-value supplier purchases, conforming to UCP 600, and can be issued in favour of the foreign manufacturer or freight agent. The cleared L/C reduces direct exposure but adds documentary costs and requires a bank quarantine of the remittance until presentation of compliant documents (invoice, bill of lading, packing list, certificate of origin). For low-value e-commerce outbound payments (e.g., third-party logistics, SaaS subscriptions), the ULC may use its bank's API-driven FX forward contract and batch payment initiation via a linked Canadian-registered payment provider; however, all outbound payments must be screened against OFSI and Canadian sanctions lists and must include either a standard purpose code or a written reference to the underlying sales contract. The ULC treasury must maintain at least one active operational account at a Schedule I bank to receive payment-clearing returns from card networks (Visa/Mastercard) settlement via the PSP (Stripe or Affirm), and then sweep these balances daily to the primary operational account to maintain a single liquidity buffer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forwards (deliverable) with a designated Canadian Schedule I bank dealer, subject to CSA derivative reporting obligations and standard ISDA/CMTA documentation

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies underlying the furniture supply contracts, provided the NDF is executed with a bank dealer licensed under Bank Act and the ISDA governing law is Ontario or English law

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) between CAD and the trade settlement currency (e.g., USD, CNY, EUR) to mitigate long-term price exposure on large-ticket furniture procurement; requires appropriate OTC derivative margin posting under the Canadian Derivatives Agreement and EMIR-equivalent reporting if the non-resident counterpart is a qualified entity
FX options (call/put) through a regulated Canadian bank dealer when the ULC desires non-linear protection without dilution of profit margin
Zero-cost collars (risk reversals) for moderately volatile currencies, combining capped downside with limited upside protection, all executed under a BoC-regulated dealer's master FX agreement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Business Corporations Act Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 50 late-filing penalty; continued non-compliance may lead to administrative strike-off or dissolution by the Registrar after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and Alberta corporate tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's taxation year-end; balance-due due two months after year-end, or three months for qualifying CCPCs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; compounding daily interest; directors may be personally liable under the Income Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST Return (if filing period is annual)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: One month after the end of the reporting period; annual filers use the period end shown on the CRA account
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty ranges from 1% to 8% of the balance due plus daily interest; repeated default triggers higher penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, a private ULC must appoint an independent auditor at each annual meeting unless all voting shareholders consent in writing to waive the audit for that financial year. There is no revenue or asset threshold for private companies; a reporting issuer is always required to have an independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises and reporting issuers; private corporations may use Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook (ASPE) or IFRS. The chosen framework must be applied consistently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Alberta Corporate Registry annual return confirms the registered office and current directors. Share transfers must be recorded immediately in the Register of Members; the individuals with significant control (ISC) register must be updated within 15 days of any relevant change and its accuracy confirmed at least annually at the time of the annual return, with offences for false or omitted entries.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$ 7,500 – US$ 18,000 if an independent audit is engaged; waiver available by unanimous shareholder consent

stage_6.entry_description: Registered legal name, 9-digit Business Number (BN) and corporate account 'RP' designation, tax year-end, Alberta jurisdiction of incorporation, Article of the ABCA under which the ULC was formed.
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned ULC remits Part I tax under BN RP account; file T2 electronically via CRA E-file (mandatory for corporations with gross revenue > CAD 1,000,000); provide the name and address of the US beneficial owner.
